title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. rho is an element of SL(2,Z) of order 6, apparently rho = (0 1; -1 1), so rho^3 = -1 and rho^{-1} = (1 -1; 1 0). The notation rho(g) means the conjugate rho g rho^{-1}. Because rho^3 = -1 is central, conjugation by rho is an automorphism of order 3 of GL(2, Z^) and of each GL(2, Z_l).

Equation (87) is g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1. Expanding gives g rho(g) rho^2(g) = (g rho)^3 rho^{-3} = -(g rho)^3. So (87) is equivalent to (g rho)^3 = -1. Equivalently, it is the 1-cocycle (norm = 1) condition for Z/3 acting on GL(2) through this conjugation. The solutions of the form lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} are exactly the coboundaries.

The previous page classifies the l-adic solutions:
- det g = delta with delta^3 = 1;
- case 1°: c + d - b = 1, a 2-parameter family, split into the subcases a+b != 0 and a+b = 0 (the latter involving a primitive cube root of unity u);
- case 2°: g = -delta^{-1} rho^{-1}.

The struck first lines check the example -rho = (0 -1; 1 -1).

Remark 1°. -rho is a solution, since (-rho)^3 = 1, just as -rho^{-1} is. But -rho falls under case 1°: c + d - b = 1 - 1 + 1 = 1. Meanwhile -rho^{-1} is the exceptional case 2°.

Remark 2°. To solve (87) in GL(2,Z^) = prod_l GL(2,Z_l), choose for each l an l-adic solution using the results (86). The case labels 1°-3° may differ from one l to another. Cases 1°, 2°, 3° give families with 2, 1 and 0 parameters.

Remark 3°. This is an open question: does every solution in SL(2,Z^) have the parametric form (58), lambda_0 rho(lambda_0)^{-1}, or the twisted form lambda_0' tau_0 rho(lambda_0')^{-1}? The twist tau_0 is built from a matrix like (-1 . ; . 1). It suffices to check each SL(2,Z_l)' separately. Grothendieck is unsure whether the answer changes without the condition g = id mod 2, which only concerns the 2-adic component. The marginal NB records related parametrisations such as g = lambda_0^{-1}... and g = -lambda_0... for the other equations.

Answer to the question (modern argument). Apart from g rho = -1, i.e. g = -rho^{-1}, which can never be a coboundary, (g rho)^3 = -1 forces g rho to have characteristic polynomial x^2 - x + 1. So Z_l^2 becomes a module over Z_l[zeta_6] = Z_l ⊗ Z[zeta_6]. This is the maximal order, a DVR or a product of two copies of Z_l, so the module is free of rank one. Hence g rho is GL(2,Z_l)-conjugate to rho, i.e. g = lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} with lambda in GL_2. Descending to SL_2 is obstructed by Z_l^x / N(Z_l[zeta_6]^x). This quotient is trivial for l != 3 and of order 2 for l = 3, where the prime is ramified. So the twisted second family is needed exactly at l = 3, and the mod-2 condition plays no role. The next page indeed concludes that excluding the case A+B = 0 / -rho^{-1}, one is in the generic two-parameter case.
errors: Remark 1° first read '(tout comme rho^{-1})'. But rho^{-1} is not a solution, since (rho^{-1})^3 = -1. The corrected statement 'tout comme -rho^{-1}' is the right one.

The worry about the hypothesis g = id (2) is unnecessary. Z_2[zeta_6] is an unramified DVR, so every solution is already a coboundary 2-adically. The only genuine obstruction to an SL_2-coboundary (as opposed to a GL_2 one) is at l = 3.

The previous page's transcription writes rho^{-1} as (-1 1; 1 0), which has determinant -1. This is inconsistent with the next page's -rho^{-1} = (-1 1; -1 0). The consistent value is rho^{-1} = (1 -1; 1 0).

ideas.what: Recasting g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1 as (g rho)^3 = rho^3 = -1, i.e. as a 1-cocycle condition for Z/3 acting by conjugation on GL(2, Z^)
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian 1-cocycles for a cyclic group; conjugacy classes of torsion elements
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to Esquisse / Longue Marche discussions of order-2/3/6 relations in the Teichmüller tower; not this computation

ideas.what: Question whether every solution is a coboundary lambda rho(lambda)^{-1} (up to a twist), checked prime by prime l
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of H^1(Z/3, SL_2(Z_l)) / classification of order-6 elements in SL_2(Z_l) via lattices over Z_l[zeta_6]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Latimer–MacDuffee type correspondence; local class numbers)

ideas.what: Case analysis of l-adic solutions into families depending on 2, 1, 0 parameters, with the case allowed to vary with l
ideas.modern_name: Local (adelic) parametrisation of solutions of a profinite 'loop equation' in its linear/abelianised shadow

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine local computation in a linearised (GL_2) shadow of the loop/hexagon relations. The open question Grothendieck raises has a standard answer via lattices over Z_l[zeta_6]: obstruction only at l = 3, no role for the mod-2 condition. It is a nice archival detail, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Remark 2°: 'il suffit de choisir pour rho une telle solution' should read 'il suffit de choisir pour [chaque] l une telle solution dans GL(2, Z_l)'. Likewise 'peuvent varier d'un l à un autre', not 'd'un rho à un autre'.

Remark 1°: the surviving text is 'Évidemment -rho est aussi solution de (87) (tout comme -rho^{-1}), mais il est justiciable du cas 1°)'. The '(tout comme rho^{-1})' line belongs to the crossed-out version.
The struck top formula concerns g = -rho = (0 -1; 1 -1), for which g^3 = -rho^3 = 1. Reading it as 'g^3 = rho^{-3} = -1 = (0 -1;1 -1)' conflates the matrix with the scalar.

'(58) = lambda_0(-1/2) rho(lambda_0)^{-1}' is likely lambda_0 times a small matrix (entries -1, 1) times rho(lambda_0)^{-1}, i.e. the twisted form lambda_0' tau_0 rho(lambda_0')^{-1}, not a fraction -1/2.
'J'ignore [?] = si on n'a pas g = id (2)' probably reads 'J'ignore ce qu'il en est si on n'a pas g ≡ id (2)'.
